packets.title: Cloudflare Worker: beta-tester feedback intake
packets.responsibility: The entire trust boundary described in CLAUDE.md §6: the ONLY holder of the GitHub write-scoped token (GITHUB_FEEDBACK_TOKEN, a Cloudflare Worker secret, never sent to or readable by the browser), fronting POST /issue and POST /attachment for both desktop and web builds. Issues land on ISSUE_REPO (mysteropodes/nemo, Issues:write); attachments land on the separate ATTACHMENT_REPO (mysteropodes/strokemotion-feedback, Contents:write) so a leaked token can never reach the source tree. Runs looksLikeSpam server-side (link-count, phrase-list, repeated-char/word heuristics, explicitly script/language-agnostic) since spam arrives as a direct POST, bypassing any client-side check. CONFIRMED (grep, zero matches): src-tauri/src/lib.rs's old submit_feedback_issue/upload_feedback_attachment commands are actually gone from current source, not just documented as removed — desktop now routes through this same Worker exclusively (via tauri_plugin_http, per worker-feedback/README.md's own 2026-09 note), matching CLAUDE.md §6's history.
packets.writer: hand-edited directly (worker-feedback/src/index.js, wrangler.jsonc); no app module writes to this packet. Deployed via `wrangler deploy` from worker-feedback/, a separate trigger from the root Worker.
packets.public_api: POST /issue { title, body, labels } -> creates a GitHub Issue. POST /attachment { filename, contentBase64 } -> commits to attachments/<filename> in ATTACHMENT_REPO, returns its raw.githubusercontent.com URL. OPTIONS -> CORS preflight (204). Any other method -> 405. Any other path -> 404.
consumers: src/js/feedback-bridge.js — confirmed by grep: desktop calls via window.__TAURI__.http.fetch (tauri_plugin_http, bypasses both the webview CSP connect-src and this Worker's own CORS allowlist, neither of which lists tauri://localhost), web calls via plain fetch(); both hit workerPost() -> POST /issue (line 421) and POST /attachment (line 371). Not covered by C06 or C07's scope_files (checked directly) — feedback-bridge.js itself remains uncovered by any merged or in-flight census as of this writing, outside this packet's bounded ownership to claim.
packets.oracle: none found — confirmed by two independent greps (`find` for *worker*test*/*test*worker* across the repo, and C08's own earlier tests/** grep) that no test file exercises worker-feedback/src/index.js. See DEF-2.
packets.notes: Proposed C16 together with C15.native.web-deploy-worker (see cross_cutting_notes). Higher priority than its file count (3) suggests: it is the app's only outbound-write-credential surface, and this census found it to also be undertested (DEF-2) and under-documented against its own live config (DEF-1).

packets.title: Cloudflare Worker: static web app deploy target
packets.responsibility: FULLY CHARACTERIZED this census — C08's draft explicitly left this 'not read in depth' / 'unknown writer, unknown public_api'. It is an assets-only Worker (root wrangler.jsonc: `"main": "worker/index.js"`, `assets.directory: ./src`, custom domains nemomotion.org / www.nemomotion.org) serving the static site via the ASSETS binding, with exactly one dynamic route: /api/google-font, a same-origin proxy for live Google Fonts lookups. The proxy's reason to exist: fonts.googleapis.com's /css2 response depends on request User-Agent (modern UA -> .woff2, old-Android UA -> a plain .ttf on fonts.gstatic.com), and browsers forbid overriding User-Agent from fetch() — so this must run server-side. The redirect target host is pinned to fonts.gstatic.com before being fetched, since the URL is read out of the upstream response rather than built locally. Separately, EVERY response from this Worker (both the proxy and the ASSETS passthrough) gets a fixed set of security headers (CSP with no script-src/style-src by explicit, commented design choice — the app needs unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval/wasm-eval — plus frame-ancestors/object-src/base-uri, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS), added 2026-08 after an audit found the site sent none at all.
packets.writer: hand-edited directly; no app module writes to this packet. Deployed via `wrangler deploy` from the repo root, triggered by .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml (already covered by C08's tooling-and-ci area, cross-ref only).
packets.public_api: Any HTTP method reaching /api/google-font triggers handleGoogleFont (no explicit method gate, unlike feedback-worker-service's POST-only check — factual asymmetry, not flagged as a defect: the route has no side effects, it only proxies a read). Every other path/method falls through to env.ASSETS.fetch(request).
consumers: src/js/vector-text-bridge.js's fetchGoogleFontWeight — confirmed by grep (function at line 396, calls fetch('/api/google-font?...') at line 408, invoked at lines 428-429). The desktop equivalent, fetch_google_font (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:89, registered as a Tauri command at :221), is out of this packet's bounded ownership — cross-ref only, already excluded per C08's draft.
packets.oracle: none found (same two-grep confirmation as the feedback-worker-service packet). See DEF-2.
packets.notes: Supersedes C08's draft packet C08.native.web-deploy-worker (same 2 files, 'genuinely un-characterized' in the draft). C04b's own scope_files already lists worker/index.js as a cross-reference ('same UA-spoofed relay idea, outside this census') without claiming it — confirmed no overlap. Proposed C16b, fold into C16 alongside feedback-worker-service: both are small Workers with real routing/security logic and zero tests, a materially different shape from the config-only C15 packets above.

cross_cutting_notes: Methodology: every file in all 5 draft packets was existence-checked against the live tree at 391f2e3 (ls, matching exact byte sizes for the two binary-shaped files). Every consumer claim was re-derived via grep with line numbers rather than trusted from C08's draft prose or from source comments alone — this caught the feedback-bridge.js coverage question (checked directly against C06/C07 scope_files: uncovered) and confirmed the vector-text-bridge.js / fetch_google_font call sites precisely. Both Worker source files (worker/index.js, 101 lines; worker-feedback/src/index.js, 199 lines) were read in full end-to-end, not sampled — the draft had explicitly flagged worker/index.js as its 'lowest-confidence packet, not read beyond existence'.

The C15/C16 split proposed by C08's own draft ('may become C15-C16', carried into this issue's title) is confirmed here as the right cut, not just plausible: C15.native.src-tauri-build-and-config + ffmpeg-sidecar-binary + nemo-mcp-build-metadata is pure 'verify config/binary/manifest currency', zero application-code reading, one shared oracle family (npm run doctor). C15.native.feedback-worker-service + web-deploy-worker are two independent Cloudflare Workers with real routing/CORS/security-header/spam-filter logic and (per DEF-2) zero test coverage — a materially different risk and skill shape. Each half comfortably fits its own 30-90 minute work-size budget alone; combined, acting on DEF-1/DEF-2 in the worker half would likely exceed one leaf's budget.

DEF-1 and DEF-2 are the substantive findings of this census, not the packet split: both were found by directly reading source/config end-to-end and diffing against each other, not inherited from the draft (the draft only flagged the *absence* of an oracle for feedback-worker-service; it did not read wrangler.jsonc against README.md, and it did not read worker/index.js at all).

One documentation-accuracy correction against C08's draft, unrelated to DEF-1/DEF-2: the draft implied ffmpeg's provenance is documented in both THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES_RUST_TAURI.txt. Only the former actually covers it (confirmed by direct read of both files); the latter has zero ffmpeg mentions. The required documentation is accurate and complete — this is a miscount in the draft, not a gap in the repo.

known_defects.summary: worker-feedback/README.md documents ALLOWED_ORIGINS as a single origin ('currently https://nemo-editor.mysteropodes-auth.workers.dev'), but the live worker-feedback/wrangler.jsonc actually sets three, comma-separated: https://nemomotion.org, https://www.nemomotion.org, https://nemo-editor.mysteropodes-auth.workers.dev. The wrangler.jsonc file's own inline comment dates the custom-domain additions to 2026-08-28 ('nemomotion.org is the custom domain (2026-08-28); the workers.dev origin is kept during the transition'), so the README was accurate when written and has not been updated since that config change. Low severity (this is the CORS allowlist for a Worker whose actual behavior is governed by the live wrangler.jsonc, not the README — no security impact, but the README is the only human-facing 'how do I change this' doc for the one file in the whole repo that gates the app's sole outbound GitHub write credential, and it currently under-describes the live allowlist by two origins.
known_defects.severity: documentation drift (config source of truth is correct and unaffected; the operator-facing README for a security-relevant Worker is out of date, confirmed by direct read of both files, not inferred)

known_defects.summary: Neither Cloudflare Worker in this area has any automated test coverage. worker-feedback/src/index.js is the app's SOLE holder of a write-scoped GitHub token and runs the only server-side spam filter (looksLikeSpam) gating what reaches a public issue tracker — its filename-validation regex (path-traversal guard for attachment commits), CORS-origin matching, and spam heuristics are all untested. worker/index.js sets the CSP and other security headers for the ENTIRE deployed web app on every response, and its /api/google-font route has no HTTP method restriction — also untested. C08's draft had already flagged the absence of an oracle for feedback-worker-service specifically ('none found... flag for a follow-up oracle, given it handles a write-scoped secret'); this census confirms that gap is real (re-grepped, still zero matches) and extends it to web-deploy-worker, which the draft had not read closely enough to make the same call.
known_defects.severity: test-coverage gap (security-relevant: one Worker gates the app's only outbound write credential, the other sets site-wide CSP; confirmed by direct repo-wide search, not merely re-stated from the draft)
